newsitem.title: UK: Labour's Blair says UK entry into EMU "a big if".
newsitem.headline: Labour's Blair says UK entry into EMU "a big if".

text.p: Tony Blair, leader of Britain's opposition Labour party, reaffirmed on Monday that he saw formidable obstacles to Britain joining a single European currency in the first wave.

In his only set-piece foreign policy speech of the six-week campaign for the May 1 election, Blair also sounded doubtul about whether Britain would be in a position to sign up for the single currency during the next five years.

"If a Labour government were to decide to enter a single currency in the course of the next parliament -- and that is a big if -- I give my word that there will be a referendum before we are committted to entering," he said in a speech.
Blair said there must be genuine and sustainable convergence between the economies of countries that did take part in economic and monetary union.
"It is in neither our nor any other European country's interests that there should be fudging or fiddling of the rules and we will have no truck with a fudged single currency."
The Labour leader said that ruling out membership forever would destroy any influence Britain had over the process.
"Therefore we will keep our options open. And when we make our decision, we should do so on the basis of a hard-headed assessment of our national economic interest."
Blair portrayed Labour as the only British party capable of taking a lead on Europe and said the ruling Conservative party was hopelessly divided over the issue.
